dedupe_keys.name: green infrastructure site prioritisation for urban flood resilience in monterrey and brussels frugisp model

description: This case study is a Scientific Reports paper that introduces the Flood Resilience-based Urban Green Infrastructure Site Priority model, FRUGISP, and applies it to Monterrey in Mexico and Brussels in Belgium, two cities with very different features that both face flooding. The model is a GIS-based multi-criteria assessment that ranks urban regions for green infrastructure by their flood resilience level and by land available for building it. Results map the regions of highest priority in each city, and the authors argue the approach can be applied elsewhere to guide decision makers in choosing locations for green infrastructure projects that reduce urban flood impacts. Coverage: two cities, with priority maps, not a downloadable dataset on the page read. Access: free article; the article is CC BY 4.0; any data or code release was not checked. Caveats: only the abstract was read, so criteria, weights and validation are not summarised. It supports spatial planning of stormwater green infrastructure and adaptation studies, and lists no linked catalogue records.
